A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same H-EPM research and contain 17 readable pages, including appendices A–F. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original inference and RL experiments, component ablations, ACEBench evaluations and token-entropy measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports the proportion of actions executed without guidance in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: The memory graph, edge weighting, adaptive retrieval and memory-guided RL procedure are unchanged. Masking and discarding guidance were already described in v2; the expanded Appendix C.5 explains these existing choices.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same τ-Bench, τ²-Bench, ToolSandbox and ACEBench coverage, including online memory construction without an available training set. No domain or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines: ReasoningBank, ToolNet and retrieval for inference; GRPO, SFT and AgentEvolver for RL; and GNN4Plan in the retrieval ablation. ACEBench retains Retrieval Top-1.

E3.justification: The splits, metrics, model configurations and training budgets in Section 5.1 and Appendix E are unchanged. The expanded masking discussion does not report revised experimental conditions.

E4.justification: The component, weighting, retrieval, rollout, entropy and masking-versus-discarding studies remain unchanged, as do the case studies. Appendix C.5 expands interpretation of the existing comparison rather than adding an ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or revised repeated-run practices. The new percentage of unguided actions is an outcome, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Appendix C.5 newly states that over 70% of actions receive no added guidance, quantifying v2's description of a 'large fraction' in Section 5.3. All numerical entries and rankings in Tables 1–10 are retained.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, memory definitions and edge-weight equations are unchanged. The new discussion of training mismatches is qualitative and introduces no formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The hybrid-memory and RL contributions, generalization claims and stated improvement magnitudes remain the same. Replacing 'experience-induced self-evolution' with 'experience-evolution' changes terminology without changing claim scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 newly distinguishes rollout–update and train–test mismatches and explains the preference for masking through sparse guidance and reuse of the agent's successful trajectories. v2 only described the alternatives and their performance ordering. Appendix F's limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer to the abstract. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts and implementation settings are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. Changes to the Huang survey entry and NaviAgent reference are bibliographic updates rather than additions of distinct works.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: abstract terminology, removal of a general sentence in Section 2.2, two explanatory paragraphs in Appendix C.5, and correspondence and bibliographic edits. The section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v3 rearranges the author lines, adds a proceedings notice and a recurring 'Title Suppressed Due to Excessive Size' header, and reflows opening and appendix pages. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–10 retain their content, captions and basic display structure.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer improves reproducibility information, while Appendix C.5 makes the rationale for the existing masking choice more explicit and quantifies guidance frequency. These are limited documentation gains: benchmark evidence is unchanged and the causal explanation receives no separate validation. The new placeholder running headers slightly reduce presentation polish.
